Key Message 1...Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms
expected today into tonight. Isolated showers and thunderstorms
are possible Monday.

A high pressure ridge at the surface and aloft continues to
exit E'ward this morning. In the wake of the ridge, cyclonic 
W'erly to NW'erly flow aloft and embedded shortwave troughs 
impact Western and Central NY the rest of today through Monday.
At the surface, a primary low should wobble ENE'ward across 
northern ON, James Bay, and northern QC today through early 
Monday evening. Accordingly, a warm front should drift NE'ward 
across our CWA this afternoon through evening and usher-in a 
warmer and more humid air mass originating over the Gulf. A cold
front should then sweep E'ward through our region tonight 
through about midday Monday. Behind the cold front, a lake-aggregate
trough lingers over the eastern Great Lakes and vicinity, 
including our CWA, as a ridge attempts to build from the Upper 
Midwest and vicinity. 

Fair weather is now expected to persist through daybreak in our
CWA. Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms with 
periods of heavy rainfall are expected late this morning through
tonight as weak to perhaps moderate CAPE, including elevated 
CAPE, is released by the following: moist isentropic ascent 
along the upper-reaches of the warm front, low-level 
convergence/moist ascent along the surface warm and cold fronts,
and as downshear gust fronts interact favorably with low-level 
vertical wind shear amidst primarily moderate deep-layer bulk 
shear. Cannot rule-out a severe storm or two capable of producing
damaging straight-line wind gusts this afternoon and early 
evening, when diurnal convective mixing of the boundary layer 
amidst peeks of sunshine should yield appreciable boundary layer
CAPE and DCAPE near 500-700 J/kg per latest trends in higher-res
model soundings. Behind the cold front, isolated rain showers 
should occur tonight into Monday since subtle shortwave troughs 
and attendant surface trough axes will traverse Western and 
Central NY generally from west to east. Low-level convergence 
and moist ascent along the surface trough axes should release at
least weak potential instability in the lowest ~1 km AGL. A few
thunderstorms are possible Monday afternoon and early evening, 
when the same lifting mechanisms may release weak boundary layer
CAPE stemming from daytime warming. Showers and thunderstorms 
on Monday should end by sunset, following the onset of boundary 
layer stabilization via nocturnal cooling.

High temperatures should reach the mid 70's to mid 80's this
afternoon. The warmest highs are expected along the lake plains
and the middle and northern portions of the Genesee Valley. Lows 
should reach mainly the upper 50's to mid 60's around daybreak 
Monday. Late afternoon highs should reach the 70's to lower 80's
on Monday, behind the weak cold front.

Key Message 2...Dry weather likely Monday night and Tuesday.  

High pressure ridging at the surface and aloft should build 
from the western Great Lakes and vicinity Monday night through 
Tuesday. Stabilizing subsidence accompanying the ridge is 
expected to promote dry weather. Considerable clearing and weak 
or calm surface winds accompanying the ridge should contribute 
to lows reaching the 50's to lower 60's around daybreak Tuesday.
Steam fog should form in the river and lake valleys of the 
Western Southern Tier, Finger Lakes, and Eastern Lake Ontario 
Region during the predawn hours of Tuesday morning. Patchy
radiation fog should also form, especially inland from Lakes
Erie and Ontario, amidst lingering low-level moisture from the
expected rainfall. Fog will dissipate via the onset of diurnal 
convective mixing of the boundary layer shortly after daybreak. 
Highs are forecast to reach the 70's to lower 80's late Tuesday 
afternoon.

Key Message 3...Another round of isolated to scattered showers and 
thunderstorms forecast for the midweek period.

The above-mentioned ridge at the surface and aloft exits E'ward
Tuesday night and allows a warm front to sweep N'ward through
Western and Central NY. Simultaneously, cyclonic W'erly flow
aloft becomes established over our area and embedded shortwave
disturbances traverse Western and Central NY. The cyclonic
W'erly flow aloft and embedded shortwave disturbances should
continue to affect our area Wednesday through Wednesday night,
and a cold front should sweep E'ward through Western and 
Central NY. Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms are 
expected after midnight Tuesday night through Wednesday night as
weak to perhaps moderate CAPE, included elevated CAPE, is 
released by the following: moist isentropic ascent along the 
upper-reaches of the warm front and ahead of shortwave trough 
axes; low-level convergence and moist ascent along the surface 
warm front, surface cold front, and surface trough axes 
attendant to the shortwave troughs. Overnight lows should reach 
mainly the mid 50's to mid 60's T
